DenebLab AbcVersion 1.2.19

Usage: abcversion [command] [options]

Commands:
  (default)    Get version information for the current repository

     Examples:
       abcversion
       abcversion --path ./my-repo
       abcversion --project MyLib
       abcversion --scope src/MyLib
       abcversion -p semversion
  init         Initialize .abcversion.json in current git repository

     Examples:
       abcversion init
       abcversion init --force
  info         Show diagnostic information about version resolution

     Examples:
       abcversion info
       abcversion info --path ./my-repo
       abcversion info --project MyLib
       abcversion info --scope src/MyLib
  projects     List configured projects from .abcversion.json

     Examples:
       abcversion projects
       abcversion projects --path ./my-repo

Options:
  --path <path>        Which repository to read (default: current directory).
                       A locator, not a filter: naming a subdirectory still
                       versions the whole repository. Use --scope to narrow.
  --project <name>     Project name from .abcversion.json (default: main)
  --scope <subdir>     Narrow the commit count to a subdirectory, without a
                       .abcversion.json entry. Relative to the repository
                       root. Cannot be combined with --project.
  -p, --property <name>  Get only one property (e.g. semversion, gitsha)
  --version            Show version
  -h, --help           Show this help

Example .abcversion.json:

  {
    // Base version for the entire repository.
    // All branches and projects will use this as a starting point unless overridden.
    // It used in version repository without projects and branches
    "BaseVersion": "0.3.0",

    // With projects, you can define multiple projects in the same repository,
    // each with its own versioning scheme.
    "Projects": {
      // Project name. This is an arbitrary identifier for the project.
      "server": {
        // Path to the project relative to the repo
